analysis.title: Is AI Eating The Ad Dollars That Pay For AI? Goldman's Delta-One Boss Is Starting To Wonder
key_insights: Market focus has shifted from capex durability to value capture: who earns the returns and how the AI investment cycle is financed. Goldman EMEA delta-one head Rich Privorotsky says cash flow is under pressure and financing needs are rising.
Demand held up (AWS +39%, Azure +48%, Google Cloud beat) but hyperscaler stocks fell anyway, because the market is now questioning financing and returns.

Amazon: AWS grew 39.3% to $46bn, ahead of consensus but perhaps light of whispers. Capex is $220bn this year and 'meaningfully more' in 2027. Advertising grew 12% to $19.6bn vs 18% expected, the first miss in seven quarters. Trailing FCF is negative $42bn. The stock fell roughly 10% after hours.
Amazon burned $33.5bn of FCF in Q3 vs $7.7bn outflow expected, on quarterly capex of $77.3bn, and raised $48.1bn of new long-term debt in the quarter.

Alphabet posted a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow. Search grew 12% vs 14% expected. Goldman's US sales trading desk said this 'will likely feed share-loss narrative'. The stock was down 11% premarket.
Microsoft beat with Azure +48% and launched a $25bn bond deal the next morning, its first since 2017.

The cash funding the buildout at the two biggest spenders comes mostly from advertising, and both missed on ads. Privorotsky asks whether AI could eventually cannibalize the advertising economics financing the investment cycle. Reddit said 'AI mode does not drive traffic'.

Privorotsky hedges: Prime Day timing explains part of Amazon's ad weakness, management guided ads back to high-teens growth in Q4, and AI may stimulate commercial search, so it is 'probably premature to extrapolate'.
Reddit fell as much as 12% after hours as US daily users slipped to 50.7 million from about 53 million last quarter.

Intel fell 20%+ overnight after guiding Q4 revenue to $15-16bn vs about $17bn expected. Data center and AI revenue grew 78% and server CPU demand exceeds supply, while PC demand contracts on memory inflation. Intel does not expect positive cash flow this year.

Oracle investor day: path to positive FCF in H2 FY28 and $30bn+ in FY29, capex stepping down in FY29, non-GAAP operating margin of 40%+ by FY30 on $225bn+ revenue, and incremental capital raises capped at $20bn through FY30 excluding refinancing. The stock rose about 10%. Privorotsky called it arguably the most important development for credit, though still need to see spreads respond.

Goldman Credit MarketStrats (Reid Zhou) reports client sentiment of 'a crisis without a crisis'. Long equity/short credit and decomp are the consensus medium-term trades, with credit (especially cash) viewed as an asymmetric short at current valuations. Zhou personally likes fading this by selling AI CDS against NDX puts.

Zhou's sequence of AI scares in credit: February private credit (AI disruption), July hyperscaler supply, now the ability to afford higher funding costs. He expects the next wave to focus on demand and ROI.
Cost of credit protection for hyperscalers has risen significantly in the last month relative to equity. Goldman's 3Y AI CDS basket has gone nearly vertical while NDX puts barely moved.

Goldman credit strategists (Lynam, Grut, Ali) say price action since mid-October shows a threshold beyond which AI cost-of-capital concerns can threaten the broader growth narrative. USD credit correlations are at their highest since the Q1 Iran escalation. They expect BBs to absorb the brunt of AI-related financing, prefer carry in B-rated, stay neutral on HY AI-related credit (especially project finance) and underweight CCCs.

Thursday tape: Goldman's AI basket fell 1.5% while S&P ex-AI rose 1.5%, with AI used as a source of funds (Gail Hafif). S&P closed down 0.3% at 7,720 on a $9bn MOC buy imbalance, SPX volume 35% above the 20-day average. Someone bought 15,000 SPX March 5500 puts, nearly 30% below spot.

Asia overnight looks like a potential outright gross unwind: KOSPI about -3.5%, TWSE -2.5%, AI winners down 3-5% while consumer and AI laggards caught a bid. Shanghai Composite near 3,600, about 15% below the May peak and near one-year lows.

Macro backdrop: Tehran reportedly rejected mediated overtures and reiterated seven conditions, Trump canceled some weekend campaign appearances, and midterms are next week. Privorotsky: 'it's understandably difficult to add risk.'

Privorotsky's near-term call is to 'chop with light positioning and bearish sentiment', with the post-election period a 'chance to climb wall of worry'. He says financing constraints have not yet changed capex spending intentions. The ZeroHedge authors disagree and expect credit to force discipline first.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand is resilient: AWS +39%, Azure +48%, backlogs remain resilient, Oracle shows a path to positive FCF, and the post-election period could be a chance to climb a wall of worry (Privorotsky).
tension_points.bear_case: Capex keeps growing while ad engines and free cash flow weaken, pushing the financing bill onto the bond market, with credit protection costs rising faster than equity hedges.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Financing constraints forcing capex discipline, which Privorotsky says is not yet visible in spending intentions.

tension_points.bull_case: Prime Day timing explains part of Amazon's ad weakness, ads are guided back to high-teens growth in Q4, and AI may stimulate commercial search activity.
tension_points.bear_case: Two ad-funded spenders both missed on ads, and Reddit says AI mode does not drive traffic, so AI could cannibalize the ad economics financing the cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Amazon's Q4 ad growth guided back to high-teens failing to materialize.
